The left branch is composed of resistor R1 and source E1 in series; the middle branch is resistor R3, and is labeled with a downward current I3; the right branch is composed of resistor R2 and source E2 in series. In the figure, the source polarities of E1 and E2 are opposite. Reasoning: The problem gives I3 = 0 A, so there is no voltage drop across the middle resistor R3, and therefore the voltage between the upper and lower common nodes is 0 V. Since the source polarities of the left and right branches are opposite, when writing KCL at the top node and the middle branch has no current, the magnitude of the left-branch current E1/R1 must equal the magnitude of the right-branch current E2/R2, that is, E1/R1 = E2/R2.
